result.markdown: # Writing to a file ![](/images/R_writing.png){style="width:200px; background:white; border-radius:5px" fig-align="center"} Data can be read into an R object by [reading](/files_subsetting/reading.qmd). Data in an R object can be saved to a file by __writing__. ## Parks data frame Before we __write__ data to a file we will create a new __data frame__ from "parks_df". First I like to create a new __variable__ from our old __variable__ if there are many steps. This means if we make a mistake we can go back and recreate the new __variable__. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} parks_t_df <- parks_df ``` ::: Next step we will create a new column called "Total_species". ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} parks_t_df$Total_species <- rowSums(parks_df[,3:8]) ``` ::: ::: {.callout-note} I am including many ways to subset columns as reminders. Normally I wouldn't have so many different ways in one command. We are using "_" instead of spaces in our column names as R doesn't particularly like spaces in column names. We will see how to use spaces later. ::: The final step before writing is to transpose the __data frame__ leaving out the Park name and State columns: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} #Transpose dataframe parks_t_df <- t(parks_t_df[,3:9]) #Check structure str(parks_t_df) #It is not a dataframe #Let us therefore convert it to a data frame parks_t_df <- as.data.frame(parks_t_df) #Structure check str(parks_t_df) ``` ::: ## Writing to a csv file Now we'll __write__ the __data frame__ to a file called "Park_species_info.csv". When __reading__ from a file I prefer `read.csv()`, however when writing to a file I prefer `write.table()`. With this __function__ we will include the option `sep=","` to have commas as the column separators. We will also include the option `col.names=NA` to create an empty space above the row names. If this was not included then the first column name would be above the row names. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} write.table(parks_t_df, file = "Park_species_info.csv", sep = ",", col.names=NA) ``` ::: Have a look at the file contents with RStudio. ## Writing to a tsv file Let's do it one more time with the Global ecological footprint info. First __read__ in the file again in case you do not have it. Then transpose the __data frame__ and ensure the resulting object is a __data frame__: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} #Read in global_eco_footprint_df <- read.csv("Global_eco_footprint.tsv", row.names = 1, sep = "\t", check.names = FALSE) #Transpose ensuring output is a data frame global_eco_footprint_t_df <- as.data.frame(t(global_eco_footprint_df)) ``` ::: __Write__ the __data frame__ to a tab delimited file (.tsv). This time we will make it so the row and column names are not surrounded by quotes: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} write.table(global_eco_footprint_t_df, "Global_eco_footprint_transposed.tsv", sep = "\t", col.names=NA, quote = FALSE) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: :::
